AI infrastructure supply-demand gapAI基础设施供需缺口
×13 · 50 steps
AI infrastructure supply is structurally constrained vs exponential demand growth. Global AI compute power demand is projected to rise from 83 GW in 2023 to 532 GW by 2031, but supply only from 39 GW to 253 GW, leaving a widening gap. Hyperscaler capex surged 87% Y/Y and is expected to remain elevated (~$1.2 tn in 2027), driving tightness in data center capacity, memory, cooling, and power infrastructure. US data center construction is limited by labor to 12–35 GW/year, while TSMC, Intel, and ASML ramp equipment capacity by 30%+. AI contract pricing is rising 25% on renewals, and CoreWeave backlog reached $104 bn. AI debt issuance is straining credit markets, with spreads widening 30 bp YTD.

China consumer demand weakness中国消费需求疲软
×10 · 40 steps
China domestic consumption is weakening across multiple discretionary categories. Online sales declined yoy across beer (-28%), white goods (-19%), beauty (-12%), etc. Retail sales growth slowed to 0.6% YoY in July, with apparel -1%. Auto sales plunged -22% in August. Weakness is broad-based: NEV orders fell sharply (BYD -50%, NIO -72%), smartphone shipments declined 26%, cosmetics online growth slowed to 5%. Stimulus effects are fading: trade-in subsidies added only 90bp to H1 retail and then reversed. Consumer sentiment remains subdued with K-shaped divide between premium and mass-market. Multiple earnings cuts across consumer durables, sportswear, and collectibles.

AI component supply tightnessAI组件供应紧张与定价权
×7 · 33 steps
AI demand is creating persistent supply shortages across semiconductor and electronic components, driving price hikes and margin expansion for suppliers. DRAM and NAND prices have surged 482-860% Y/Y, high-end AI CCL/PCB is in short supply, and packaging substrates (ABF) are undersupplied by 7-19% through 2028. Foundry capacity is tight (SMIC utilization ~95%), and semiconductor equipment lead times have lengthened to 8-9 months. Component shortages are expected to last into 2026-2027, giving pricing power to suppliers with capacity.

    Mechanism

    Conclusion
    After two months of materially softer jobs and inflation data, a hike at the September meeting has become very unlikely barring a dramatic shift in the tone of the August data due in early September; under our baseline economic forecasts the inflation news is more likely to improve further than to deteriorate anew as the year progresses, and we still think market pricing for the funds rate is too hawkish.

J.P. Morgan5 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    A model sits on the Pareto frontier when peers cannot provide higher capability at the same or lower price, or comparable capability more cheaply; models inside the curve face a harder commercial position as users can choose a stronger or cheaper alternative.
    830e8d408ec5·《GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek's repricing shift the capability-cost frontier; raise Zhipu/MiniMax PT, remain OW/Neutral》·2026-08-18
  2. 2
    Premise
    DeepSeek is the clearest Chinese example of structural cost leadership, with low pricing supported by model architecture and system-level efficiency across MoE, attention design, KV-cache requirements, quantization and serving optimization, giving it flexibility to decide how much efficiency improvement to pass through to users and how much to retain through monetization.
    830e8d408ec5·《GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek's repricing shift the capability-cost frontier; raise Zhipu/MiniMax PT, remain OW/Neutral》·2026-08-18
  3. 3
    Mechanism
    DeepSeek announced on Aug 13 a repricing effective Aug 17 that raises selected V4 API prices substantially (V4 Pro Peak-hour input from Rmb 3.00 to Rmb 9.00, cache-hit input from Rmb 0.03 to Rmb 0.30, output from Rmb 6.00 to Rmb 27.00) while remaining among the more competitive high-capability choices on price, suggesting its previous pricing contained meaningful monetization headroom.
    830e8d408ec5·《GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek's repricing shift the capability-cost frontier; raise Zhipu/MiniMax PT, remain OW/Neutral》·2026-08-18
  4. 4
    Conclusion
    JPMorgan prefers Zhipu over MiniMax because Zhipu's latest competitive improvement (GLM-5.3) is internally generated and more defensible, whereas MiniMax's near-term improvement comes from a competitor's DeepSeek repricing decision and can reverse; Zhipu's thesis requires continued model iteration rather than relying on GLM-5.3 alone.
    830e8d408ec5·《GLM-5.3 and DeepSeek's repricing shift the capability-cost frontier; raise Zhipu/MiniMax PT, remain OW/Neutral》·2026-08-18

    Premise
    Industry is undergoing a paradigm shift from compute centric AI to memory centric AI; Sandisk management and Tenstorrent CEO stated memory capacity and memory bandwidth is the main limitation to compute, and NAND is the most optimal solution for inference given inference emphasis on read (vs write) and the explosion of context memory (KV-cache).
    17f328bab6eb·《Memory & Storage: Why Sandisk investor day makes us more bullish on SNDK; Reiterate Outperform TP $3000》·2026-08-15
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    HBF (High Bandwidth Flash) promises to be a game changer for AI and the memory industry with the bandwidth of HBM and the capacity of NAND; HBF could require 3x to 4x the wafer capacity per Exabyte (Bernstein estimates) due to additional on-chip space, which could significantly eat up wafer supply and lead to shortages continuing far longer than even the bulls expect.

PBOC monetary easing framework transition中国央行宽松与利率框架转型
×5 · 22 steps
The PBOC is transitioning to a rate-based framework, narrowing the overnight repo corridor to 50bps and shifting the operating target to DR001. Despite no LPR cuts, corporate loan rates dropped to 3.05% in June 2026, with 50.8% of loans priced below LPR. The PBOC uses positive fixing errors to slow RMB appreciation and deepens the offshore CNH market via Southbound Bond Connect quota expansion (RMB500bn to 800bn), supporting RMB internationalization.

Deutsche Bank4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Over the past decade, China has undertaken one of the most significant monetary policy framework reforms among major economies, transitioning from a quantity-based framework toward a more market-based one across four phases: pre-2015 quantity framework, 2015-2019 interest-rate liberalization, 2019-2024 MLF-linked LPR system, and 2024 onward transition to overnight repo.
    ce9a9c7c8d1e·《China: Modernizing the monetary policy framework》·2026-08-20
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Monetary policy modernization in China has been less about replacing quantitative tools with policy rates than about rebalancing their relative importance, with market-based interest rates now playing an increasing role in policy implementation and transmission while structural and quantitative instruments continue to support broader policy objectives and financial stability considerations.
    ce9a9c7c8d1e·《China: Modernizing the monetary policy framework》·2026-08-20
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    China has moved substantially towards a more interest-rate-centric framework, but the transition remains incomplete — the interest-rate corridor is still evolving, multiple policy objectives continue to shape implementation, and quantitative as well as structural tools remain important alongside policy rates; the next phase of reform is likely to focus less on building new instruments and more on improving how policy signals are transmitted through financial markets and the broader economy.
    ce9a9c7c8d1e·《China: Modernizing the monetary policy framework》·2026-08-20
  4. 4
    Conclusion
    If transmission improves as intended, the adjustment could occur in two stages: in the near term, further PBoC easing could keep the 5-year NDIRS low or push it lower; over the medium term, evidence that policy easing is gaining traction should lift expectations for nominal growth and the equilibrium policy rate, supporting a repricing of medium-term interest-rate expectations and a widening of the currently compressed 2Y-5Y NDIRS slope toward levels more consistent with other Asian markets.
    ce9a9c7c8d1e·《China: Modernizing the monetary policy framework》·2026-08-20
HSBC4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Some commercial banks recently rolled out corporate loans priced off DR001, following the first batch in the Hainan Free Trade Port; the pilot gives corporates an alternative to LPR-linked lending and signals a new channel for monetary policy transmission.
    508f24447172·《Tech frictions, steady trade》·2026-08-14
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Under the current framework, policy rate changes feed through to LPR quotations monthly; a DR-linked structure could improve transmission efficiency because DR001 reflects interbank funding costs on a daily basis. The move follows the recent PBoC announcement to introduce overnight reverse repo operations and narrow the interest rate corridor, which could help control volatility of front-end interbank borrowing costs.
    508f24447172·《Tech frictions, steady trade》·2026-08-14
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    Several DR-based loans are arranged as one-year facilities referencing the three-month average of DR001; adding disclosed spreads of 87bp and 164.32bp implies lending rates of roughly 2.23%–3.00%. By contrast, the one-year LPR has remained unchanged at 3.00% for 14 consecutive months.
    508f24447172·《Tech frictions, steady trade》·2026-08-14
  4. 4
    Call
    HSBC thinks DR-linked loans are likely to only complement rather than replace LPR-based loans, as the model is better suited to large corporates, short-tenor financing and cross-border trade; SMEs, mortgage loans and longer-term corporate funding will likely remain dependent on LPR-linked loans.
    508f24447172·《Tech frictions, steady trade》·2026-08-14

BernsteinDissent4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Merck and Moderna announced that their personalized mRNA cancer vaccine, intismeran autogene (mRNA-4157/V940, in combo with Keytruda), met both the primary endpoint of recurrence-free survival (RFS) and the key secondary endpoint of distant metastasis-free survival in a Ph3 melanoma trial, representing the first successful late stage validation of a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine platform.
    db7133b4fb8f·《Weekend Healthcare Pulse: understanding Merck/Moderna's breakthrough - what INTs are and the potential (and challenges) ahead》·2026-08-21
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Previous generations of cancer vaccines pursued a 'one therapy for all patients' approach targeting a handful of common tumor antigens shared across broad populations, whereas Moderna/Merck's platform follows a 'one patient, one therapy' model designed around each individual's mutational fingerprint, with the underlying manufacturing process remaining standardized though every vaccine contains a different sequence.
    db7133b4fb8f·《Weekend Healthcare Pulse: understanding Merck/Moderna's breakthrough - what INTs are and the potential (and challenges) ahead》·2026-08-21
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    Melanoma alone is unlikely to become a mega-blockbuster market - more likely low single-digit billions; however, if efficacy can be replicated in NSCLC, RCC, bladder cancer and earlier-stage solid tumors, personalized neoantigen vaccines could evolve from a ~$1-2 Bn melanoma opportunity into a platform exceeding $10 Bn across multiple solid tumor indications.
    db7133b4fb8f·《Weekend Healthcare Pulse: understanding Merck/Moderna's breakthrough - what INTs are and the potential (and challenges) ahead》·2026-08-21
  4. 4
    Conclusion
    The key challenge is reproducing melanoma success in other tumor types - melanoma is among the most immunogenic cancers with high tumor mutational burden and abundant neoantigens; the true test will be indications such as NSCLC, RCC, bladder cancer, and eventually colder tumors with lower mutation burdens like CRC, where generating a sufficiently strong immune response may be more difficult.
    db7133b4fb8f·《Weekend Healthcare Pulse: understanding Merck/Moderna's breakthrough - what INTs are and the potential (and challenges) ahead》·2026-08-21

Logic Chains by Firm2 firms · 7 steps · every step verified verbatim against the source
Deutsche Bank4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    A 21% current-account gap is not the same thing as a 21% undervalued currency: the IMF's -21.3% REER gap measures how much the REER would need to appreciate if exchange-rate adjustment alone were required to close the current-account surplus, not a direct estimate that the RMB is 21% below fair value.
    a732f3b64669·《RMB: Imbalance ≠Valuation ≠ Adjustment》·2026-08-14
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    The IMF's two direct FX valuation models are much more muted than the CA approach: the REER-Level model finds the RMB undervalued by only 2.7%, the REER-Index model concludes the RMB is fairly valued at 0.5% above its historical benchmark, and DB's FX Research Team estimates undervaluation of only 3-8% against a trade-weighted basket.
    a732f3b64669·《RMB: Imbalance ≠Valuation ≠ Adjustment》·2026-08-14
  3. 3
    Mechanism
    Chinese corporates increased FX purchases and reduced FX settlement in recent years to hold more FX assets outside China and avoid a weak, low-yielding currency, with the total gap amounting to almost USD800bn between 2022 and H1 2025; this muted the normal link between rising trade surplus and RMB appreciation, and the RMB began to strengthen from H2 2025 onward as FX-hoarding flows ended.
    a732f3b64669·《RMB: Imbalance ≠Valuation ≠ Adjustment》·2026-08-14
  4. 4
    Conclusion
    Without domestic adjustment, a nominal appreciation intended to close the relative-price gap could deepen the domestic forces—weak demand, deflation and low profit margins—that created the CA surplus in the first place; it would worsen domestic absorption and push Chinese manufacturers further toward export markets, eroding any initial gains from currency appreciation.
    a732f3b64669·《RMB: Imbalance ≠Valuation ≠ Adjustment》·2026-08-14
Goldman Sachs3 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    On our estimates, the RMB is at least 20% undervalued, and China's ongoing gains in manufacturing competitiveness—the ongoing decline in China's producer prices relative to US or global producer prices—boost that number every year unless the nominal exchange rate appreciates commensurately, making it hard to see how external balance could ever be achieved without a large nominal exchange rate appreciation.
    c40f75dd23b0·《They're Not Hiking》·2026-08-17
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    The weakness in China's domestic demand already threatens to push growth well below potential, and a stronger RMB would take an additional toll; the classic solution to this quandary—first suggested by Australian economist Trevor Swan in the 1950s—is an exchange rate appreciation combined with a domestic demand boost (e.g. via an expanded social safety net that makes consumers more comfortable spending); such a combination could move China's economy closer to external balance without undermining growth and employment.
    c40f75dd23b0·《They're Not Hiking》·2026-08-17
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    China's large and growing current account surplus suggests RMB appreciation is warranted to support external rebalancing, while policies that boost domestic demand are needed for internal rebalancing; these measures may not be sufficient for global rebalancing but are necessary steps in the right direction.
    cfc2d91290c9·《China: Three things in China》·2026-08-17

Goldman Sachs5 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    Launch acts as the upstream chokepoint for the space economy because only a limited number of launch-service providers exist globally, and the cost of placing one kilogram into LEO fell from $65,400/kg on the US Space Shuttle in 1981 to $1,500/kg on SpaceX Falcon Heavy today as partially reusable rocket boosters converted fixed rocket-building costs into an asset reusable across launches.
    d13c927ff179·《The Second Space Age》·2026-08-18
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Reusable launch systems, smaller satellites, advances in computing and modern manufacturing techniques have fundamentally shifted the economics of reaching space, allowing private-sector companies to build infrastructure once exclusive to government programs while capital markets provide critical funding.
    d13c927ff179·《The Second Space Age》·2026-08-18
  3. 3
    Mechanism
    The report's key data project $1.4tn in global commercial space revenue by 2030, $700bn in global value from Earth observation data by 2035, a 25x reduction in launch costs since 1981, 600+ global ground stations, 65% of economic value generated by GPS since 1980 and 3.9x growth in space-launched objects since 2010.
    d13c927ff179·《The Second Space Age》·2026-08-18
  4. 4
    Conclusion
    Governments are increasing domestic space and defense investment: US Department of Defense space funding is expected to reach $57.7 billion in fiscal year 2026, the administration's 2027 proposal requests $71 billion, Golden Dome is estimated by the White House to cost $175 billion through 2028, the European Space Agency plans to increase investment by 31% over three years, and China's space-sector investment rose from $340 million in 2015 to $2.9 billion in 2024.
    d13c927ff179·《The Second Space Age》·2026-08-18
  5. 5
    Call
    As space companies enter public markets, capital-market activity is expected to intensify, potentially increasing M&A and supporting space as an institutional asset class while lower launch costs encourage orbital specialization and the movement of terrestrial services into space.
    d13c927ff179·《The Second Space Age》·2026-08-18

Logic Chains by Firm2 firms · 10 steps · every step verified verbatim against the source
Bernstein5 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    China's economy remains under pressure: while exports have stayed relatively resilient, domestic demand has been a persistent drag, with retail sales growth largely stagnating at around 0-1% YoY and new vehicle sales down c.20% YoY in 2026 YTD.
    22cc92ddbd4d·《Asia Consumer Blast: How to Revive China's Economy? Lessons from Henry Ford》·2026-08-22
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Policy tools such as consumer subsidies and trade-in programmes have generated only a temporary boost to demand before effectiveness fades; over time, consumers have become conditioned to expect lower prices or future government incentives, encouraging them to postpone purchases.
    22cc92ddbd4d·《Asia Consumer Blast: How to Revive China's Economy? Lessons from Henry Ford》·2026-08-22
  3. 3
    Mechanism
    The property market remains depressed, consumer confidence subdued, and deflationary pressures persistent in China despite repeated stimulus measures.
    22cc92ddbd4d·《Asia Consumer Blast: How to Revive China's Economy? Lessons from Henry Ford》·2026-08-22
  4. 4
    Conclusion
    The author argues that despite years of stimulus efforts and weak consumer confidence, perhaps China's problem is not that people are spending too little but that they are working too much; Henry Ford's century-old approach of higher wages, shorter working hours, and more time to consume may still hold lessons today.
    22cc92ddbd4d·《Asia Consumer Blast: How to Revive China's Economy? Lessons from Henry Ford》·2026-08-22
  5. 5
    Call
    MaintainOutperformTarget price130.00 HKD
    BYD Company (1211.HK): rating Outperform; target 130.00 HKD; reference 91.80
    22cc92ddbd4d·《Asia Consumer Blast: How to Revive China's Economy? Lessons from Henry Ford》·2026-08-22
Goldman SachsDissent5 steps
  1. 1
    Premise
    China's July activity data: industrial production rose 4.5% yoy supported by robust exports; retail sales grew only 0.6% yoy; fixed asset investment contracted 6.7% yoy in the first seven months of 2026, implying double-digit year-over-year declines in July.
    2a39424036d7·《From Weak to Weaker》·2026-08-22
  2. 2
    Mechanism
    Weekly steel production has fallen in July and early August while steel prices (especially rebar) have declined in recent months; the combination of lower volumes and lower prices points to weak demand as the cause of slowing economic growth.
    2a39424036d7·《From Weak to Weaker》·2026-08-22
  3. 3
    Mechanism
    The 'anti-involution' campaign that started last July lifted prices in steel and polysilicon for several months, but without solid demand and with labor market stability concerns preventing significant supply cuts, prices fell back to similar or below pre-campaign levels.
    2a39424036d7·《From Weak to Weaker》·2026-08-22
  4. 4
    Conclusion
    Despite weak July activity data and downside risk to Goldman's Q3 GDP forecast, Goldman still believes the government will manage to achieve at least 4.5% official real GDP growth this year and meet its target, barring extraordinary external shocks; the government has missed its growth target only twice since reform (1998 Asian Financial Crisis, 2022 Omicron).
    2a39424036d7·《From Weak to Weaker》·2026-08-22
  5. 5
    Conclusion
    Without demand-side stimulus and fundamental reforms to unleash domestic demand, cyclical weakness could turn into structural hysteresis; if the cautious, intermittent style of policy response persists for a few more years, prolonged financial stress on households, private businesses, and local governments could impair future growth potential.
    2a39424036d7·《From Weak to Weaker》·2026-08-22

  1. 1
    Premise

  2. 2
    Mechanism
    In the next couple of weeks Qatar is approaching the point where continued absence of Hormuz transits will likely force a shutdown or a material reduction in liquefaction capacity utilization, pushing recovery of supply into the Northern Hemisphere winter.
    739986129c63·《Global Macro Outlook and Strategy: Global Rates, Commodities, Currencies and Emerging Markets》·2026-08-18
  3. 3
    Conclusion
    The largest supply shock on record produced only average price outcomes, as inventory draws were much smaller than anticipated and the loss of demand proved far greater than expected; non-OPEC oil supply growth reached 2.44 mbd year-on-year—the strongest pace recorded so far this decade—led by the US, Brazil, Canada, and Guyana.

Watching for the pre-crash 'hot sector, narrow rally' pattern
Strongest sector: Biotech (XBI), but market participation is broad — no sign of the 'single hot sector, narrow rally' warning pattern.
XBI 63-day excess return +21.6pp (96th percentile of 10 years) · Market breadth at the 97th percentile (broad participation) · XBI +25.1% above its 200-day MA (94th percentile)
Thresholds calibrated on a single event — the 2026-06/07 semiconductor selloff (n=1)
Trigger rule details
The three observed quantities
Sector relative strength = how far a sector's return has beaten the broad market's over the trailing quarter (a price proxy for crowding)
Market breadth = how many stocks participate in the rally (equal-weight index underperforming cap-weight = narrowing breadth)
% above 200-day MA = how far price sits above its own 200-day moving average (the standard BIAS technical indicator)
How the light is decided
🔴 Red: hottest sector's relative strength enters the top 5% of 10 years (≥95) AND market breadth narrows into the top 10% (≥90) — both must hold
🟡 Amber: relative strength ≥95 but breadth only to ≥60; or either relative strength or 200-day bias enters the top 1% (≥99)
🟢 Green: everything else
Once red has fired, it doesn't snap straight back to green: it must exit the top 20% (relative strength) or the top 60% (breadth) before returning to green, resting on amber in between (anti-flicker)
Any missing data shows “No data” — it never defaults to green
